## Reproduce

`python3 test/parity/interface-closure/breakdown/breakdown.py 0298d6208 HEAD build/ledger-breakdown` from the repository root (baseline `0298d6208` = integrate-042 54220fb62 + ledger-autobind-int, the first TOTALS line 5862/12234 + 2 designed out; about 6 minutes cold: closure_history.py walks the 1,899 mapping revisions, then testrefs parses every Go test). Files: `breakdown.py`, `closure_history.py`, `testrefs/main.go` under `test/parity/interface-closure/breakdown/`. Copies: `docs/parity/gap-closure/ledger-breakdown*`.

## Reading the numbers (limits, stated)

- Class 1 "Go symbol added since base" (1,219 rows) is a symbol-existence test on the baseline file text (declared top-level name, member token present). A moved or renamed Go file reads as new; the script cannot prove the mutation check per row (lane rules require it).
- Class 2 (marker on an existing test) is 0: no interface-ledger row's evidence tests are `// pi:` marker tests. Markers belong to PORT_MAP rows (portmap-check), not to interface rows.
- Class 3 includes rows a lane ported by hand and the detector later re-derived, when the Go symbol already existed at the baseline.
- Retarget (class 5) takes precedence over class 1-3; designed-out (class 4) takes precedence over retarget. 36 of today's 383 designed-out rows were ported at the baseline.
- The behaviour check is a lower bound: any asserting Go test in the target's or an evidence test's package that mentions the member (or top-level) name counts as a touch.
